title: Sunny Deol Returns to the Courtroom After Damini. Akshaye Khanna Is the Reason He Has To.
excerpt: Netflix unveils Ikka — a legal thriller that reunites two '90s icons on opposite sides of a murder trial. Streaming July 10.
body:
There's a scene seared into the memory of every '90s Bollywood kid: **Sunny Deol** in a courtroom, veins popping, voice cracking the walls, delivering the "tareekh pe tareekh" monologue in *Damini* that turned a legal drama into a full-body event. That was 1993. Thirty-three years later, the man is walking back into a courtroom. And this time, the case is personal.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=zCEWn4eCDd8</youtube>

**Netflix** has officially unveiled **Ikka**, a legal thriller that pairs Sunny Deol with **Akshaye Khanna** in what is being positioned as one of the streamer's biggest Hindi originals of the year. The film premieres on **July 10**, and it marks Sunny Deol's very first Netflix original — his streaming debut, essentially, after decades of being a theatrical force.

The setup is gorgeous in its cruelty: Deol plays a celebrated, morally spotless lawyer who is arm-twisted into defending a murder accused played by Khanna — a man whose career he had personally and notoriously destroyed years earlier. If he loses, he forfeits everything he holds dear. If he wins, he saves a man he despises. Every frame of this premise drips with dramatic poison.

> "What drew me to Ikka was the opportunity to tell a courtroom story that focuses as much on personal relationships and emotional dilemmas as it does on the pursuit of justice." — Director Siddharth P. Malhotra

Directed by **Siddharth P. Malhotra** — who delivered the acclaimed **Maharaj** (2024) for Netflix — the film comes from a place of genuine obsession. Malhotra has said this was one of the first stories he ever wanted to bring to screen, and it shows in the casting. Sunny Deol doesn't just play a lawyer; he returns to the *genre* that gave him one of his most iconic moments. And opposite him, **Akshaye Khanna** brings the quiet menace he's perfected over the last decade — think *Section 375*, think *Drishyam*, think that unsettling calm before the verdict drops.

The supporting cast reads like a masterclass in understatement. **Tillotama Shome** plays a fierce public prosecutor determined to see justice done — and if you've seen her in *Sir* or *Qala*, you know she doesn't waste a single expression. **Dia Mirza** plays the lawyer's wife, holding the family together while the courtroom tears it apart. **Sanjeeda Shaikh**, **Shishir Sharma**, and **Akansha Ranjan Kapoor** round out an ensemble that suggests this film has no intention of being a two-man show.

There's a story from the set that tells you everything about what kind of film this is. During a take, a fly hovered persistently near Sunny Deol's eye. He didn't call cut. He didn't flinch. He stayed in character, unwilling to break Tillotama Shome's rhythm. "That kind of conviction," Dia Mirza noted at the Netflix slate announcement, "sets the tone for everyone else."

## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

If you grew up watching Sunny Deol in *Damini*, *Ghayal*, and *Border*, and now you're settled in Jersey City or Brampton or Birmingham, this one's designed for you. It's on Netflix — no hunting for theatrical showtimes, no waiting for OTT windows. July 10, press play. The film also features **Akshaye Khanna** in villain mode, reportedly appearing back-to-back with his antagonist turn in the upcoming **Mahakali**, making this a remarkably productive period for an actor who spent years being criminally underused.

Written by **Althea Kaushal** and **Mayank Tewari**, and produced by **Alchemy Films**, Ikka has everything a courtroom thriller needs: impossible choices, shifting loyalties, two leads with decades of unfinished business, and a verdict that will linger long after the credits. The courtroom genre in Bollywood has been dormant for too long. If this film lands the way its pedigree suggests, Sunny Deol might just own it again — thirty-three years after the first time.
